sn40.1:0.3: A Question About the First Absorption
sn40.1:1.1: At one time Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
sn40.1:1.2: There Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed the bhikkhus:
sn40.1:2.1: “Just now, reverends, as I was in private retreat this thought came to mind:
sn40.1:2.2: ‘They speak of this thing called the “first stage of meditation”.
sn40.1:2.3: What is the first stage of meditation?’
sn40.1:2.5: ‘It’s when a bhikkhu, fully withdrawn from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and dwells in the first stage of meditation, which has the delight and contentment born of seclusion, with thinking and considering.
sn40.1:2.6: This is called the first stage of meditation.’
sn40.1:2.7: And so … I was entering and remaining in the first stage of meditation.
sn40.1:2.8: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by sensual pleasures beset me.
sn40.1:3.1: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,
sn40.1:3.3: Don’t neglect the first stage of meditation, brahmin! Settle your mind in the first stage of meditation; unify your mind and concentrate it in the first stage of meditation.’
sn40.1:3.4: And so, after some time … I entered and dwelled in the first stage of meditation.
sn40.1:3.5: So if anyone should be rightly called
sn40.1:3.6: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”
